question: GQ-007
subject: back to books — a second want-list, aimed at the tiers Shaan named
why_now: Six turns of gates checking gates, and the last two found bugs only in the gates themselves. The Library has not grown since the 78 books. The mission is books, not scaffolding.

a_selection_i_rejected.what: the Library's thinnest subjects overall — Sea stories 399, Psychological fiction 387, War stories 361, and juvenile fiction throughout
a_selection_i_rejected.why_rejected: his tier list says fiction and juvenile are "store but do not extract". Mining them would add volume against his stated priorities.
a_selection_i_rejected.instead: searched for thin subjects inside the tiers he named take-first

availability_probed_before_building.note: availability varies 46x across three subjects — worth measuring rather than assuming a subject with few holdings has many candidates

want_list.excluded: 10 — mostly Polish academy bulletins carrying a bare rights assertion

different_from_the_first_list: the first was 72 formal-designation of 81. This one is 84 institutional-review of 111 — HathiTrust and Princeton copyright determinations rather than Creative Commons marks. Same gate, different evidence grade.
dedup_now_covers_both_sources: checked against 74,752 titles including the 78 IA books already held

final_result.every_failure_was_mine_again: BAD_BODY is the transient-truncation signature; not one book was actually unavailable
